en: Proud is the rain on the cliffs
The ʻāhihi lehua flower of the uplands
Farewell to you, farewell to you
O fragrant one who dwells in the deep dark blue [?]
The fond remembrance that has come
You indeed are my beloved sweetheart
Alert to the beauty of the leaf bud
notes: Stanza breaks: the import's stanzas do not follow the song. The chorus is 2.1-2.4 plus 3.1 ('Until we meet again'); the second verse is 3.2-4.2; the third verse is 4.3-5.2. The editor may want to re-divide orig (and en with it) into verse 1 (4 lines), chorus (5), verse 2 (5), verse 3 (4).
lines 2.3 and 3.1: 'One fond embrace,' and 'Until we meet again' are in English in the original (Liliʻuokalani's own words); kept as they are.
line 1.3: the source gives the variant '(uhai)' beside 'hahai'; both mean to follow, chase, pursue. Kept as one line.
line 1.4: ʻāhihi is a kind of lehua (ʻōhiʻa) blossom; 'o uka' is 'of the uplands, inland'.
line 2.2: 'lipo' is the deep blue-black of depths or of distant forest; 'noho i ka lipo' can be 'dwelling in the dim (forest) depths'. 'Onaona' is fragrant, also gentle, sweet.
line 2.4: 'A hoʻi aʻe au' is literally 'and I return (go back)': taken as 'before I go'.
line 3.4: 'manawa' is time, and also the seat of the feelings (literally the fontanelle); here 'my heart, my feelings', though 'my time' is a possible reading.
line 4.2: 'A loko e hana nei' is elliptic: 'within, working now', i.e. stirring inside me. Sense uncertain.
Maunawili: a place on windward Oʻahu, kept as a name.
